transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-02
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~49 minutes
Recorded: Yes
Attendees: Sophie Martinez (Redwood AE), Jordan Lee (Redwood SE), Amira Patel (CISO, Ember Tech), Tom Grayson (Head of Infra), Leah Kim (Legal), Ravi Shah (ML Eng)

Summary:
Quick security posture discovery focused on Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment options, SOC2 / ISO status, SSO / SAML and SCIM, RBAC, audit logs and retention, encryption (KMS/BYOK) and data residency. Agreed next steps to share SOC2 artifacts, VPC deployment guide, and run a SE-led benchmark/poc.

Topics:
- SOC2 / ISO certification status and evidence
- SSO/SAML, SCIM provisioning, RBAC patterns
- Audit logs: content retention, SIEM integration, log schema
- Encryption at rest / in-transit; BYOK / HSM options
- Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs (latency, data control, cost)
- Retention policy for user content and telemetry

Transcript body:
[00:00] Sophie Martinez: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros?
[00:12] Amira Patel: Sure, Amira here, CISO at Ember Tech. We're trying to evaluate options for running an LLM-backed product and have a bunch of security/compliance questions.
[00:23] Tom Grayson: Tom, infra. We run mostly in GCP, VPC-only. Our main asks are auditability, encryption keys control, and getting a clear data retention story.
[00:33] Sophie Martinez: Awesome. Jordan from our SE team will walk through the posture and answer infra questions.
[00:36] Jordan Lee: Hi all, hi Amira, Tom. I'll jump in and start with where Redwood stands on certifications - SOC 2 Type II is completed for our hosted service, ISO 27001 is in progress and we expect cert note this quarter - apologies if that's spelled wrong in notes - but we can share the report.
[00:55] Leah Kim: Will you share the actual SOC 2 report or just a summary? Legal will need the full attestation and any subservice orgs.
[01:05] Sophie Martinez: We can share the SOC2 Type II attestation and the controls matrix under an NDA. For hosted customers we provide the SOC document; for Dedicated/Private we can support per-customer attestations in larger contracts.
[01:20] Amira Patel: Ok, good. What about data retention - we don't want customer prompts or PII retained beyond a certain window.
[01:29] Jordan Lee: By default our hosted API retains telemetry for X days for quality and abuse monitoring - I won't quote the number off the top of my head - but for enterprise customers we have options to disable retention, and dedicated/private deployments can be configured to not persist request bodies at all. We also offer log forwarding so you can ingest audit logs into your SIEM.
[01:48] Ravi Shah: Can you clarify "not persist"? Even ephemeral cache like KV cache, prefix caches - are those stored?
[01:56] Jordan Lee: Good callout. The KV cache is in-memory on the serving nodes; for hosted we may persist aggregated cache metrics, not raw prompts. For Dedicated and Private we can configure runtime to not write KV/prefix cache to disk and to limit any telemetry. There's sometimes imperfect transcriptions of the caching term - so it's K V cache, ephemeral.
[02:15] Tom Grayson: Encryption at rest - we need BYOK for keys, HSM-backed KMS, and rotation policies.
[02:25] Jordan Lee: We support customer-managed keys (BYOK) for Dedicated and Private deployments; for Hosted we offer KMS integration with cloud KMS and optional HSM depending on the region and plan. Key rotation and access is logged in the audit trail.
[02:40] Amira Patel: Audit logs - what events do you capture? Admin actions? Model rollouts? API keys usage? Token-level usage?
[02:49] Jordan Lee: We capture admin console actions (rollouts, permission changes), API key creation/rotation, per-request metadata (request id, model, route, token counts) and error traces. We can ship either raw logs or structured events to your SIEM via streaming. Retention is configurable per contract; we typically keep audit logs longer than request payloads.
[03:10] Leah Kim: Do you support SSO - SAML or OIDC - and SCIM for provisioning?
[03:18] Sophie Martinez: Yes, we support SAML SSO and OIDC for the console, plus SCIM for user provisioning in Redwood Console. For Dedicated/Private we can integrate with your IdP inside the VPC and offer RBAC mapping to groups.
[03:33] Amira Patel: How granular is RBAC? We need least-privilege: billing view, dev ops, model deploy rights separated.
[03:42] Jordan Lee: Our Console supports role templates and custom roles - you can define permissions down to route-level read/write and model deploy actions. For customers with strict needs we do custom role work and can tie roles to SAML assertions or SCIM groups.
[03:56] Tom Grayson: Latency vs cost - this is where we debate hosted vs dedicated. If we go hosted but need data residency and stricter retention, how does that affect latency?
[04:06] Jordan Lee: Hosted uses our multi-tenant runtime optimized for throughput; for low-latency SLAs we recommend Dedicated reserved capacity in a region close to your users - that's predictable latency and you get isolation. Private on-prem gives the most control but at higher ops overhead. There's always a tradeoff: dedicated reduces noisy-neighbor variance but costs more.
[04:30] Ravi Shah: For benchmarks, can you run our sample prompts and measure median p95 latencies and token costs?
[04:36] Jordan Lee: Absolutely - that's a standard SE-led benchmark. We'll need a small sample set and expected concurrency. We can run on Hosted and Dedicated variants so you can compare.
[04:47] Amira Patel: About encryption - for hosted where keys are Redwood-managed, how do we ensure we can get key-access logs?
[04:55] Jordan Lee: Even for cloud-managed KMS we surface KMS access logs in the audit trail; for BYOK on Dedicated we'll write to customer KMS and the access is visible in your KMS logs.
[05:06] Leah Kim: Any pen tests or third-party assessments?
[05:11] Jordan Lee: We do regular internal pentests and third-party assessments; the SOC2 report includes penetration test attestations and policy references. We can share the scope in the docs.
[05:21] Amira Patel: Data residency - can we keep models and data in our region only?
[05:28] Sophie Martinez: Yes, with Dedicated you can pin region and with Private you control the infra. Hosted customers can also be provisioned in regional clusters for EU/NA separation. We'll need to discuss your specific regulatory requirements.
[05:40] Tom Grayson: For audit log schema - do you have an example JSON schema we can ingest into Splunk?
[05:47] Jordan Lee: Yes, we'll send the structured audit-log schema and sample events. We support JSON over Kinesis, Pub/Sub or S3 delivery, and Splunk HTTP Event Collector.
[06:00] Ravi Shah: What about model lineage and rollbacks - we need traceability from model version to rollout time and who initiated it.
[06:08] Jordan Lee: Our rollout system records user, time, model hash, and can tie to Git commits if you push via our model repo integration. That gets captured in the audit logs and in per-route metadata.
[06:22] Amira Patel: Any concerns about legal e-discovery - can you put a legal hold on logs?
[06:29] Sophie Martinez: We can implement retention overrides and legal hold policies for audit logs for enterprise plans. We'll need legal coordination for the contract.
[06:40] Leah Kim: What's the default retention for request payloads in hosted?
[06:46] Jordan Lee: Off the top of my head we hold request payloads for 30 days for the hosted trial; enterprise controls allow shorter windows or zero retention. We'll confirm exact default in the follow-up email.
[07:00] Amira Patel: Do you support deleting historical data on request?
[07:05] Jordan Lee: Yes - subject to backups and retention windows. For Dedicated/Private it's straightforward as data sits in your VPC. Hosted deletions are logged and we can provide confirmation.
[07:16] Tom Grayson: Network isolation - can your control plane talk to our private network only, or does it require egress?
[07:24] Jordan Lee: For Dedicated we can set up private peering and restrict control-plane access via IP allowlists and client certs. For Private on-prem the control plane can be customer-hosted. There are details around webhooks and callbacks which sometimes require egress; we can route callbacks through your network.
[07:44] Sophie Martinez: Quick callouts - we have SOC2 Type II, per-route telemetry, BYOK options for Dedicated/Private, SAML + SCIM, RBAC templates, audit log streaming, and configurable retention.
[07:56] Amira Patel: Sounds good. On compliance, can we have a security questionnaire answered?
[08:02] Sophie Martinez: Yes - we'll fill your standard security questionnaire and attach the SOC2 artifacts.
[08:09] Leah Kim: Contractual SLAs and data processing agreement (DPA)?
[08:13] Sophie Martinez: We'll include DPA terms in the proposal; Dedicated and Private come with stronger SLAs and custom DPA language if needed.
[08:22] Ravi Shah: One more technical question - do you support hardware-backed inferencing (certain GPU families) for determinism?
[08:31] Jordan Lee: We support a set of certified instance types; we can recommend specific instance families for consistency and provide performance profiles.
[08:40] Tom Grayson: For RBAC audits, can we export user activity reports on demand?
[08:45] Jordan Lee: Yes, activity reports and audit exports can be generated and streamed to your S3/Cloud storage for long-term retention.
[08:55] Amira Patel: Ok, let's talk timeline - we're aiming for a pilot in Q2, production later in the year. Any blockers from your side?
[09:03] Sophie Martinez: None from us - we'll send docs and propose SE benchmark times. The POC would be Hosted first for speed or Dedicated if you need immediate isolation.
[09:12] Leah Kim: Pricing - we need cost estimates for Dedicated reserved capacity and also hosted per-token rates with retention disabled.
[09:20] Sophie Martinez: I'll include those in the follow-up. Dedicated pricing includes reserved vGPU hours and a base platform fee; hosted pricing is per-token with enterprise adjustments for retention and SLA.
[09:33] Amira Patel: On the SOC2 doc - do you have a summary of scoping, subprocessors, and data flows?
[09:40] Jordan Lee: Yes, the artifact set includes the scoping appendix and subprocessor list - we'll attach those.
[09:46] Tom Grayson: Any known limitations around VPC NAT or egress for callbacks?
[09:52] Jordan Lee: Some callback patterns need outbound connectivity; we can do polling alternatives or route through your proxy. We'll document options.
[10:05] Sophie Martinez: Great. Recap of next steps: send SOC2 and security docs, VPC guide and audit log schema, schedule benchmark, send pricing.
[10:15] Amira Patel: That works. Thanks.
[10:18] Leah Kim: Thanks everyone.
[10:20] End of recording.

Notes on transcription quality: medium - a few domain terms like KV cache, BYOK, and rollout names may be transcribed slightly off.
